laws.rule: Climbing onto the Borobudur temple structure needs a ticket from the official operator, InJourney Destination Management: IDR 150,000 (about A$11.74, RBA rate of 30 October 2026), daily 8.30 am to 5 pm, including a guide and the upanat sandals that must be worn on the temple.
laws.heading: InJourney Destination Management (state-owned site operator)

local-law.note: Operator source (evidence operational for this line).

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: The Borobudur structure ticket includes a wristband, Upanat temple sandals and a tour guide; climbing is only on this ticket.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Structure visits run 8:30am to 5pm WIB; arrive 30 to 45 minutes before your start. The ground-only ticket is for domestic tourists.
culture-and-protocol.note: Price not recorded (not shown in the page text read).

layers.authority: Balai Taman Nasional Gunung Merapi (national park office) and Directorate General KSDAE, Ministry of Forestry; hazard status from BPPTKG (Geological Agency volcano centre)
layers.process: Climbing Mount Merapi is closed. A Ministry of Forestry press release of 18 May 2026 says BPPTKG still holds Merapi at Level 3 (Siaga, 'alert'), that hazards include lava avalanches, pyroclastic clouds and ejected material, and that climbing is 'tidak direkomendasikan' (not recommended) for the safety of the public and visitors. It reports about 60 illegal climbers caught in a year and one death in December 2025, and says the park office responds with warning signs, trail patrols and public outreach. The release does not name a closure decree or date, so check the park office's notices. The mountain straddles Central Java and the Special Region of Yogyakarta; this applies on both sides.

sources.title: 1.000 Pegiat Alam Hadiri Sarasehan Online Membedah (Nasib) Pendakian Gunung Merapi (18 May 2026)
sources.supports: Level 3 Siaga, climbing not recommended, illegal climbing figures (read directly 2026-11-07)

zone-requirements.note: Held on Central Java because the park office and most climbing approaches (such as Selo) are there. Status is as of the 18 May 2026 release; BPPTKG publishes the current level.
